subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory contract, by Memory Wiki as a knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but durable memory schema, conflict policy, provenance semantics, and operator UX are product boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming or mirroring the settled provenance model.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, claims, and source evidence as Memory Wiki responsibilities and keep memory-core as Markdown/search/promotion until maintainers decide a lower-level write API is needed.

options.title: Defer the resolver
options.body: Keep current Markdown, promotion, and wiki layers while collecting more production examples before accepting durable schema or UX commitments.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming or mirroring the settled provenance model.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across memory-core, Memory Wiki, docs, and plugin-boundary work, making him the best available owner for the product-boundary choice.
